newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: P&O NEDLLOYD SAYS ORDERS FIVE SHIPS.
newsitem.headline: P&O NEDLLOYD SAYS ORDERS FIVE SHIPS.

text.p: P&O Nedlloyd said on Wednesday it had ordered five container vessels for a total price of $220 million.
The ships will be built at Kvaerner's German subsidiary Kvaerner Warnow Werft GmbH at Rostock-Warnernunde in Germany and will be delivered in 1998 and 1999.
P&O Nedlloyd said various methods of financing were being considered.
The ships will be deployed on its service between Australia/New Zealand and the Mediterranean.
"The order for five container vessels is a positive sign for our new company, illustrating the strength of the recently merged entity," said Tim Harris, Chief Executive Officer of P&O Nedlloyd.

P&O Nedlloyd recently formed through the merger of P&O Containers and Nedlloyd Lines. The company operates a fleet of 112 container ships and a container fleet of 540,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU).
